title: Set 49

sentences.ko: 상사가 팀을 맡아 볼 생각 있냐고 물어봤어. 돈은 더 받는데, 내가 진짜 좋아하는 일을 하는 대신 하루 종일 회의만 하고 있게 될 거야. 물어본 사람마다 다 하라고 하고 아마 그 말이 맞겠지. 그런데 월요일에는 대답해야 하는데 아직도 모르겠어.
sentences.text: My boss asked if I want to take over the team, and it's more money, but I'd be in meetings all day instead of doing the part I actually like. Everybody I've asked says take it, and they're probably right, but I have to tell him Monday and I still don't know.

alts.text: So I got asked if I want to take over the team, and it's more money, sure, but I'd be stuck in meetings all day instead of doing the part I actually like. Everyone I've asked says take it, and they're probably right, but I gotta tell him Monday and I still don't know.

My manager asked whether I would like to take over the team, and the salary is higher, but I would be in meetings all day rather than doing the part of the work I genuinely enjoy. Everyone I have asked says I should accept, and they are probably right, but I have to give him an answer on Monday and I still do not know.

sentences.note: **take over the team** 은 남이 하던 자리를 이어받아 팀을 맡는다는 뜻입니다. **it's more money** 는 돈을 더 받는다는 말을 짧게 하는 방식으로, 급여를 굳이 따로 말하지 않습니다.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 겨우내 눈여겨보던 그 재킷을 결국 샀는데 한 번밖에 안 입었어. 옷이 이상한 건 아니고 그냥 나랑 안 어울려. 가게에서 이미 알고 있었던 것 같아. 그래서 지금은 문 옆에 걸어만 두고 아침마다 늘 입던 낡은 옷을 입어.
sentences.text: I finally bought that jacket I'd been looking at all winter, and I've worn it once. It's not that it looks bad, it's just not me, and I think I knew that in the store. So now it hangs by the door and I put on the same old one every morning.

alts.text: Remember that jacket I kept looking at all winter? I finally bought it, and I've worn it once. It doesn't look bad, it's just not me, and I think I knew that in the store. So now it hangs by the door and I grab the same old one every morning.

I finally purchased the jacket I had been looking at all winter, and I have worn it once. It is not that it looks bad, it simply is not me, and I believe I knew that in the store. It now hangs by the door, and I put on the same old one every morning.

sentences.note: **it's just not me** 는 물건이 나쁜 게 아니라 내 스타일이 아니라는 뜻입니다. 옷이나 물건 이야기에 자주 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 팀에 회의 내내 한마디도 안 하고 앉아 있다가, 끝나고 나서 내 자리로 와서 그 계획이 왜 안 되는지 얘기하는 사람이 있어. 한 시간이나 있었잖아! 결국 다음 주에 그 얘기를 내 생각인 것처럼 꺼내야 하는 사람은 나야.
sentences.text: There's a guy on my team who sits through the whole meeting saying nothing, and then afterwards he comes over to my desk to tell me why the plan won't work. You had an hour! And now I'm the one who has to bring it up next week like it's my idea.

alts.text: We've got a guy on my team who doesn't say a word the whole meeting, and then after, he's at my desk telling me why the plan won't work. You had an hour! And now I'm the one who has to bring it up next week like it's my idea.

A colleague on my team sits through the entire meeting without saying anything, and afterwards he comes to my desk to tell me why the plan will not work. He had an entire hour. And now I am the one who has to raise it next week as though it were my own idea.

sentences.note: **sits through** 는 답답해도 끝까지 자리를 지키고 앉아 있는 것을 말합니다. **bring it up** 은 어떤 얘기를 먼저 꺼낸다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 애가 방에서 네 번이나 나왔어. 물 달라고, 그다음엔 발이 아프다고, 그다음엔 상어 얘기를 해야 한다고. 겨우 문을 닫았는데도 안에서 혼자 떠드는 소리가 들리더라. 그냥 뒀어. 조용하기만 하면 된 거지, 나 다시 안 들어가.
sentences.text: He was out of his room four times. Water, then his foot hurt, then he had to tell me about a shark. And when I finally got the door shut I could still hear him in there talking to himself, so I just left it. If he's quiet, he's quiet, I'm not going back in.

alts.text: Kid was out of his room four times. Water, then his foot hurt, then something about a shark. And I finally get the door shut and I can still hear him in there talking to himself, so I just left it. If he's quiet, he's quiet. Not going back in.

He left his room four times. First for water, then because his foot hurt, then to tell me about a shark. When I finally managed to close the door, I could still hear him inside talking to himself, so I left it alone. If he is quiet, he is quiet, and I am not going back in.

sentences.note: **I just left it** 은 더 손대지 않고 그냥 내버려 뒀다는 뜻입니다. **talking to himself** 는 혼잣말하는 것입니다.

sentences.ko: 내가 이 동네를 좋아한 이유의 절반은 모퉁이에 있던 그 작은 가게였어. 그런데 주인이 바뀌더니 메뉴를 싹 갈아엎었고, 이제는 집에서도 만들 수 있는 걸 20달러나 받아. 지난달에 한 번 더 가 봤는데 둘 다 끝까지 못 먹고 남겼어.
sentences.text: That little place on the corner was half the reason I liked this neighborhood, and then it changed hands and they redid the whole menu, and now it's twenty bucks for something I'd make at home. We went back last month to give it another shot and neither of us even finished.

alts.text: Half the reason I liked this neighborhood was that little place on the corner, and then it got new owners and they redid the whole menu, and now it's twenty bucks for something I'd make at home. We gave it another shot last month and neither of us even finished.

The small restaurant on the corner was half the reason I liked this neighborhood, and then it changed hands and they revised the entire menu, and now it is twenty dollars for something I would make at home. We returned last month to give it another chance, and neither of us even finished.

sentences.note: **changed hands** 는 가게나 물건의 주인이 바뀌는 것을 말합니다. **give it another shot** 은 한 번 더 해 본다는 뜻입니다.

reviewed: 3번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분이 거의 같고 오히려 격식체 낱말(entire)을 써서, 더 짧고 구어다운 말로 다시 썼습니다.
4번 casual 이 text 와 첫 낱말 하나만 달랐습니다. 축약하고 끊어 말하는 쪽으로 다시 썼습니다.
2번 formal 의 shop 을 store 로 고쳤습니다. text 가 store 인데 formal 만 영국식으로 바뀌어 있었습니다.
3번 한국어의 "한 시간이나 시간이 있었잖아" 에서 겹치는 말을 덜어 냈습니다.
4번 한국어의 "다시는 안 들어갈 거야" 가 영어(I'm not going back in, 오늘 밤 얘기)보다 세서 "다시 안 들어가" 로 맞췄습니다.
5번 한국어의 "둘 다 다 못 먹고" 겹침을 "둘 다 끝까지 못 먹고" 로 고쳤습니다.
